title: The FSD reads the ACE views directly, while Architecture v5 allows only rwb-source-data to read them
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 37 and 45; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-05
section: A1.1 constraints; A2.1, A2.5, A2.11 and A2.15 validation rules; A2.12 and A2.16 integration points
description: The FSD constraint says source data is read only from the ACE database through the SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views, and rules R-WO-01, R-WO-05, R-WO-21, R-WO-37 and R-WO-42 name the ALS and GL systems as the systems the module touches. VR-S7-005-1, VR-S7-011-1 and VR-S7-015-1 read freshness from v_ace_batch_status, and the module needs the GL write-off posting that v_ace_write_off holds. Architecture v5 slide 37 changes 'the 30 views read by any module (ADR-010)' to 'the views read only by rwb-source-data', slide 45 answers who reads ACE data with rwb-source-data alone, and slide 13 gives the S7 row a single REST call, to P1, with an event subscription to P1. The Ownership Map records no view as S7's. The read path of the whole module is therefore undefined in the FSD.
evidence: FSD S7 A1.1 constraints; VR-S7-005-1, VR-S7-011-1, VR-S7-015-1; R-WO-01 (ALS load complete), R-WO-21 (ALS and GL return a reference); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 37 (views read only by rwb-source-data), slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the 30 views; everyone else asks it through REST or a Temporal activity), slide 13 (S7 row: T to P7, T E to P8, R E to P1); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Tables (no S7 view) and Rulings.
proposed: Carry the FSD field names as the source field names that the rwb-source-data contract returns, and build every scan, decision and posting on that contract; no view and no ACE table is read by this service. Confirm the contract fields and the freshness response with P1 before wave 4 system test.

title: The FSD posts to ALS and the general ledger from this module, while Architecture v5 gives the posting to rwb-payment
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 20 and 28; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 endpoints; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 23
section: A2.9 Post an approved write-off; A2.10 Send provision inputs to Finance; A2.11 Reconcile
description: FSD A2.9 states that the module posts the write-off to ALS and the general ledger and releases the provision, and R-WO-21 to R-WO-24 give the module the ALS reference, the rejection, the retry and the retry limit. Architecture v5 slide 20 gives rwb-writeoff 'OUT: TMP Decision: child: committee approval - Payment: postProceeds', so the posting is a step on rwb-payment's queue, and 'REST Source data: GL outcome' for the result read back. The connection matrix gives the S7 row no cell to ALS, the general ledger, P2 or P8 for a REST call, and slide 28 makes the write-off posting one of the four irreversible steps that wait for the ledger. The FSD therefore holds a posting capability that v5 places in another service, and the point of no return has two candidate owners.
evidence: FSD S7 A2.9 description and steps; R-WO-20 to R-WO-25; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (S7 OUT: Payment: postProceeds, REST Source data: GL outcome), slide 13 (S7 row), slide 28 (strict mode at write-off posting); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Endpoints (no posting operation owned by S7); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 23 (posting is the point of no return; re-post, rescan or committee on failure).
owner_role: Solution architect with the P8 owner
proposed: Keep the posting decision, the reference, the rejection, the retry and the re-post as this product's behaviour, and obtain the posting itself as a step on rwb-payment's queue with the GL outcome read back through P1; this service writes no posting entry and calls ALS or the general ledger on no path. Confirm the split with the P8 owner before wave 4 system test.

title: The Ownership Map lists one table for rwb-writeoff, while Architecture v5 gives the schema four entity groups
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20, 29 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 write_off; Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql
section: Service contract, rwb-writeoff OUT DB
description: Architecture v5 slide 20 states that rwb-writeoff 'writes schema rwb_writeoff: eligibility, committee, posting, recovery after charge-off', and slide 41 repeats the four things the service owns. The Ownership Map Tables sheet holds exactly one row for S7, write_off, and the Logical Data Model holds the same one table with eleven fields. The scan result, the committee decision per account, the posting attempts and the recovery, placement and closure records therefore have no table, no field list and no key in the register that every story's section 12.7 and every DB story is written from.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (DB writes schema rwb_writeoff: four entity groups), slide 41 (S7 owns eligibility, committee, posting, recovery after charge-off), slide 29 (one schema and login per service); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Tables: one S7 row, write_off; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 write_off DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020 only.
proposed: State the four entity groups with the key fields the rules require, fix the physical name of write_off as the one table the map holds, and write the remaining table set with the S7 DB story. Add the missing rows to the Ownership Map in the same change.

title: Slide 20 names write-off collection operations that neither the Ownership Map nor the API specification holds
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 endpoints; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4
section: Service contract, rwb-writeoff IN
description: Architecture v5 slide 20 gives the service 'IN: REST GET/POST /write-offs; POST /write-offs/{id}/submit', and slide 41 gives it the first API path /write-offs. The Ownership Map endpoints sheet holds only POST /write-off-scans and POST /write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision for S7, and the API specification v4 holds the same two paths with x-module S7. The read of a write-off, the creation of a proposal and the submission of a pack to the committee therefore have no published operation, which is what the screen and the committee workflow call.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (S7 IN REST), slide 41 (first API path /write-offs); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Endpoints: two S7 rows only; API Specification v4: /write-off-scans and /write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision only, both x-module S7.
proposed: Publish the collection operations the screen and the committee need under /api/recovery/writeoff/v1 before the contract story closes, and add them to the Ownership Map and the API specification in the same change; the existing two operations keep their paths.

title: The Finance provision feed has no interface path: P2 is outbound-only and the matrix gives S7 no cell to it
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.10; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-26 to R-WO-28; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 20; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 5.2 (P2 outbound only)
section: A2.10 Send provision inputs to Finance
description: R-WO-26 sends the provision inputs and the tax file to Finance on the month-end close, R-WO-27 retries a rejected file and R-WO-28 records the tax file reference. The FSD lists 'ALS and GL' as the integration point of A2.10. The program BRD makes P2 rwb-integration outbound-only and gives it the file windows and the GL write-off event, but the connection matrix gives the S7 row no cell to P2, and the Ownership Map holds no interface row for this service. The feed that Finance waits for at the month end therefore has no owned path.
evidence: FSD S7 A2.10 integration points; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-26, R-WO-27, R-WO-28; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (S7 row: no P2 cell), slide 20 (S7 contract: no FILE line); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 5.2 and the outbound-only statement for P2; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Interfaces: no S7 row.
owner_role: Solution architect with the integration lead
proposed: Carry the Finance feed as a product requirement with the retry and the task after the retry limit, and take the path as an open question with a named owner: a P2 interface, or an activity on another service's queue. Nothing in this document designs the file.

title: The committee pack is a document in the document hub, and the matrix connects S7 to P5 on no path
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.3, A2.5, A2.9; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-05, R-WO-09, R-WO-10; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: A2.3 Prepare the write-off pack; A2.5 Route the population; A2.10
description: R-WO-05 has the write-off agent prepare the pack including the route history, the legal and asset state and the residual; R-WO-09 holds a pack whose pack_document_id is absent and R-WO-10 routes it once the provision carried and the pack document are present. The FSD names 'the Workbench document hub' as the integration point of A2.3. The document hub is P5, whose capability is metadata, custody, retention and the retention job JOB-17, but the connection matrix gives the S7 row no P5 cell and no Temporal or REST path, so neither the pack document nor its retention class has an owned path.
evidence: FSD S7 A2.3 integration points and steps; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-05 (pack document), R-WO-09 (pack_document_id absent), R-WO-10, R-WO-47 to R-WO-48 (retention class); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (S7 row: no P5 cell), slide 44 (JOB-17 retention on rwb-document); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Workflows, Events and Jobs: no S7 to P5 row.
owner_role: Solution architect with the P5 owner
proposed: Hold the pack document in the document hub and carry its reference and its retention class here; state the call type as an open question with the P5 owner, because the matrix shows none.

title: Agency placement, result and recall run through the partner portal, which is S9 and is created in the same wave
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.15, A2.16; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-30, R-WO-33, R-WO-34, R-WO-35; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 10.2
section: A2.15 Record a customer payment after charge-off; A2.16 Sell a post charge-off population
description: R-WO-30 places the account with the agency chosen on measured return and sends the instruction 'same day on the portal', R-WO-33 attaches the result reported on the portal the same day, R-WO-34 recalls a placement on measured return or conduct, and R-WO-35 replaces it. The FSD names the partner portal as the integration point of A2.16. The partner service is S9 rwb-partner, which the program BRD places in wave 4, the same wave as this service, and the connection matrix gives the S7 row no S9 cell. Placement, result and recall therefore cannot be demonstrated until the partner contract exists, inside the same release.
evidence: FSD S7 A2.15 and A2.16 integration points; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-30, R-WO-33, R-WO-34, R-WO-35; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (S7 row: no S9 cell); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 10.2 (RWB-SVC-S7 and RWB-SVC-S9 both wave 4); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Services: S9 rwb-partner wave 4.
owner_role: Partner and agency manager with S9
proposed: Carry the placement, the result and the recall as product behaviour, hold every placement decision until the partner contract is published in the same wave, and sequence the placement slice last inside wave 4.

title: A charged-off population is handed to the debt sale route, and neither service's matrix row shows the other
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.16; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-32, R-WO-50, R-WO-51; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 10.2
section: A2.16 Sell a post charge-off population
description: R-WO-32 hands a charged-off population to the debt sale route where the placement type is sale, and R-WO-50 closes the case when the buyer settles and the data transfer completes, with R-WO-51 closing the item on the buyer's remittance. The debt sale route is S6 rwb-debtsale, created in wave 3, one wave before this service. The connection matrix gives the S7 row no S6 cell and the S6 row no S7 cell, so the hand-over that starts the sale of a charged-off book has no owned path and no direction.
evidence: FSD S7 A2.16 integration points and prerequisites; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-32, R-WO-40, R-WO-50, R-WO-51; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (S7 row: no S6 cell; S6 row: no S7 cell); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 10.2 (S6 wave 3, S7 wave 4).
owner_role: Solution architect with the S6 owner
proposed: Carry the hand-over as product behaviour with the population, the route and the approval recorded here, and take the call type and the direction as an open question with the S6 owner before wave 4 system test.

title: The FSD routing rules move the case through twenty states, while Architecture v5 gives the case state to rwb-case
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-01 to R-WO-51; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 20 and 25; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 workflows
section: A2.1 to A2.16 business rules; the states SCAN_DUE to CASE_CLOSED
description: Every write-off rule names a source state and a target state: SCAN_DUE, MONTHLY_SCAN_STARTED, SCAN_HELD, POPULATION_PROPOSED, PACK_PREPARED, PACK_INCOMPLETE, CASE_REMOVED_BY_TEAM, WITH_COMMITTEE, ESCALATED_TO_CREDIT_COMMITTEE, APPROVED, RETURNED_TO_PURSUE, DEFERRED, POSTING_PENDING, POSTED, POSTING_REJECTED, PROVISION_RELEASED, FINANCE_FEED_SENT, FINANCE_FEED_REJECTED, PLACEMENT_DECIDED, PLACED_WITH_AGENCY, PLACEMENT_RECALLED, SOLD_POST_CHARGEOFF, PAYMENT_MATCHED, PAYMENT_EXCEPTION, REMITTED_TO_BUYER, WRITEOFF_EXCEPTION, RETENTION_RUNNING and CASE_CLOSED. Architecture v5 gives the case, the CMMN state, the queues, the tasks, the timers and the parent CaseWorkflow to rwb-case, and gives this service one published event, WriteOffApproved. Which service holds which of the twenty-eight states, and which one moves the case to closed, is therefore not stated.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-01 to R-WO-51, source and target state columns; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (P3 row: T E to S7), slide 20 (S7 OUT: WriteOffApproved only), slide 25 (CaseWorkflow parent, a child workflow per stage); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Workflows: WriteOffWorkflow owned by S7, CaseWorkflow owned by P3.
owner_role: Solution architect with the P3 owner
proposed: Keep the write-off states as the stage's own record inside WriteOffWorkflow, publish the outcome and let rwb-case move the case state; state the split as an open question with the P3 owner so that no state has two writers.

title: The sources disagree on what starts the monthly scan: a Schedule, the ACE batch, or Quartz
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 12 and 23; Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-16; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 rulings
section: A2.1 description and system background event; A2.2
description: Architecture v5 slide 44 makes JOB-16 a Temporal Schedule in rwb-writeoff on the 3rd working day, and the Temporal and Drools design makes it a Schedule started on the 3rd working day after AceDataReady. The Batch and Scheduling Design v4 starts JOB-16 on the ACE batch-complete record, and the design's Phase 1 note T2 keeps Quartz. The FSD says only that the feature receives its trigger and runs monthly. The Ownership Map ruling on JOB-16 resolves the conflict in favour of the Architecture v5 catalogue and records ASM-A6-flows-12; this document carries that ruling and does not reopen it.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (JOB-16 monthly, 3rd working day, rwb-writeoff, Schedule), slide 20 (Schedule: scan, 3rd working day); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 12 (Scheduled job for JOB-16), slide 23 (starts when JOB-16 runs on the 3rd working day after EV-26 AceDataReady), and the Phase 2 item on Quartz; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Rulings: JOB-16, ASM-A6-flows-12.
proposed: Run the scan as a Temporal Schedule on the 3rd working day that also tests the ALS batch, so both the date and the data condition are met, and no Quartz table, connection or job is used; the ruling of ASM-A6-flows-12 stands.

title: The fifty-one write-off rules exist but their package has no owner and no version in force
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-01 to R-WO-51; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 the rule package item; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 27; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 rulings
section: A2.1 to A2.16 validation rules; BR-S7-001 to BR-S7-016
description: Every feature of this module applies a rule, and R-WO-01 to R-WO-51 carry the transitions. The Temporal and Drools design states that package codes are Phase 2 and that each of S1 and S3 to S9 needs one owning service for its route set, naming rwb-writeoff among them. No source read here states the package code, the version label in force, the owner of the package or the date it is promoted, so no scan can state which package it evaluated.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-01 to R-WO-51; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 (rule governance and versioning) and the Phase 2 item 3 naming rwb-writeoff among the route sets without a package; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 27 (rule governance); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Rulings (no write-off package row).
owner_role: Center of excellence analyst with P7
proposed: Read the criteria and the rules from a governed package through the rwb-decision contract, record the package and rule version on every scan and decision, and take the package code and its promotion date as an open question.

title: No source states the write-off tax criteria, the meaning of the two tracks, or the criteria version in force
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.2; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-006 and ASM-013; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-01, R-WO-03
section: A2.1 and A2.2 validation rules
description: R-WO-01 tests every open case against the eligibility rule on both tracks and against the tax criteria, R-WO-03 holds the scan where the tax criteria version is absent, and VR-S7-001-1 and VR-S7-002-1 show MSG-S7-001 until Finance publishes it. No source read here defines the criteria, names the two tracks, or states who publishes the version, and the epic BRD carries the same gap as Q-006 with ASM-013.
evidence: FSD S7 A2.2 validation rules and message MSG-S7-001; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-006 (what are the tax criteria and the two tracks) and ASM-013 (held as a versioned rule package); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-01, R-WO-03.
proposed: Hold the criteria as a versioned package read at run time, record the version on every account, and open the scan only on a published version; no criterion and no track name is asserted here.

title: The write-off exception loop has no named owner, no time limit and no field to hold either
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.12; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-007 and ASM-014; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-24, R-WO-43
section: A2.12 Work the write-off exception loop
description: The FSD states that this loop has no owner today, R-WO-24 and R-WO-43 name the exception owner only as 'Owner to confirm with C&R', and the service level column of both rules reads 'to confirm with Credit Administration'. The epic BRD carries Q-007 and ASM-014, which reads the loop as owned by the write-off team until a named owner is decided. No source gives the time limit, and the FSD field catalog holds no field for the owner or the limit.
evidence: FSD S7 A2.12 intent ('This loop has no owner today') and roles; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-24 and R-WO-43 (owner 'to confirm with C&R', service level 'to confirm with Credit Administration'); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-007, ASM-014, RISK-004.
proposed: Carry one named owner role and one time limit as required product properties, hold the owner as the write-off team until decided under ASM-014, and take the value as an open question so that the exception can be built and cannot be released without it.

title: The write-off cap the epic BRD's risk names has no requirement, no rule and no value
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 RISK-004; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-01 to R-WO-51; Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6)
section: A2.1 eligibility; A2.11 reconciliation
description: RISK-004 of the epic BRD says that the write-off cap, the tax criteria and the exception ownership may stay undecided and the population cannot be defended, and its mitigation is to hold the criteria as a package and reconcile approved to posted. No requirement, no rule of R-WO-01 to R-WO-51 and no field of this module names a cap, its basis, its period or what it applies to, and the only limit the rules carry is the write-off committee limit of R-WO-11 and R-WO-12.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 11.4 RISK-004; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-11 and R-WO-12 (committee limit only); FSD S7 A2.1 to A2.16 (no cap).
owner_role: Head of Asset Liquidity with Risk
proposed: Report the population against the cap once the cap exists, and take the cap, its basis and its period as an open question; no value is asserted here and no cap is enforced in this release.

title: The committee that decides a write-off above the limit, and the delegation behind it, are not defined
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-12, R-WO-13, R-WO-15; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-053 and Q-001; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 9 DL18; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20
section: A2.5 and A2.6 validation rules; the committee roles
description: R-WO-12 routes a pack above the write-off committee limit to the credit approval committee chaired by the product head with Risk, and R-WO-13 approves it 'inside the delegation with Risk'. The FSD gives the roles Write-off committee member and Finance and CFO delegate, and gives no further definition of who chairs, who votes or what the substitute is. The limits themselves are DL18 in the program BRD, and Q-001 of the epic BRD asks for the limit by decision, product and amount with the substitute for each. Architecture v5 makes the approval an ApprovalWorkflow child on rwb-decision with the DoA lookup as a parameter, which needs the table to exist.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-11 to R-WO-16; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-053, Q-001; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 9 DL18 (load the regulation's levels now, add names and substitutes when signed); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (TMP Decision: child: committee approval), slide 16 (approval and DoA).
proposed: Take the approval through the approval workflow with the limit read from the delegation table at run time, record the level applied and the approver role, and take the level values and the committee composition as an open question under DL18 and Q-001.

title: The FSD has no wait for the ledger acknowledgement that strict mode requires before a posting
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 28; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 23; Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.9; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-20 to R-WO-25
section: A2.9 Post an approved write-off
description: Architecture v5 slide 28 makes debt transfer, write-off posting, auction sale and title transfer wait until the central ledger confirms the decision record, and the Temporal design repeats that the write-off posting waits for the ledger. The FSD gives the posting task, the reference, the rejection, the retry and the provision release, and names no wait on any acknowledgement, so a build against the FSD alone would post on an unconfirmed record — on the one step the architecture calls irreversible.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 28 (strict mode; irreversible steps wait for the ledger acknowledgement), slide 27 (decision record and hash chain); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 23 note (write-off posting waits for the central ledger); FSD S7 A2.9 and R-WO-20 to R-WO-25 (no acknowledgement step).
proposed: Hold the posting until rwb-decision confirms the decision record in the central ledger, proceed only on that acknowledgement, and raise an alert where the ledger is late; the wait is a product requirement of this service, not a design of the ledger.

title: The case closes after a retention period that is not set, and the retention class behind a closure is not defined
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 NFR-028, NFR-031 and DL26; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012; Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.13; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-47, R-WO-48
section: A2.13 Close the case after the retention period
description: R-WO-47 closes the case only with a retention class on every document, and R-WO-48 holds the closure and raises a document task where a class is missing. NFR-031 states that case records carry a retention and archive rule by record class and that the case closes after its retention period, with the target 'Not set', and NFR-028 leaves the periods open under DL26. No source gives a period, a class list or a disposal rule for a write-off record.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 NFR-028 (retention classes defined per type; periods not set), NFR-031 (target Not set), DL26; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012; FSD S7 A2.13; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-47, R-WO-48.
proposed: Hold the closure on a retention class and a recorded period, make the period a versioned data row, and take the periods and the class list as an open question under DL26 and Q-012; no period is asserted here.

title: The FSD defers the mirrored GL fields of write_off to DEF-05, which no source read here defines
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) change note; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 write_off DF-FIN-013 to DF-FIN-020; Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql
section: Document control, change note v3; A2.4, A2.6, A2.7, A2.8, A2.12, A2.14 and A2.16 field catalog
description: The FSD v3 change note states that the write_off mirrored GL fields are left for DEF-05. The FSD field catalog lists eight fields of write_off, the Logical Data Model holds eleven, and three of them are mirrored from the general ledger: responsibility_center, cost_center and gl_product, with amount and posted_date also sourced from GL. No source read here contains DEF-05, its scope or its date, so the field set of the table cannot be closed from the sources.
evidence: FSD S7 document control, change note v3 (write_off mirrored GL fields left for DEF-05); FSD S7 A2.4.3.2 field catalog (eight fields); Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020 (eleven fields, three sourced 'GL'); Physical Schema v6.sql write_off and its comments.
proposed: Carry the eleven model fields as the field set of write_off, mark the three GL-sourced ones as mirrored and never re-keyed, and take DEF-05 as an open question so that no field is invented and none is dropped.

title: The rules require a removal reason, a review date and a pack reference that no field of the module holds
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-07, R-WO-09, R-WO-17, R-WO-18; Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) field catalog; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 write_off
section: A2.4, A2.5, A2.8, A2.12 field catalog
description: R-WO-07 removes a case on removal_reason, R-WO-09 holds a pack on pack_document_id, R-WO-17 defers on review_date and R-WO-18 refuses a decision on decision_reason and review_date. The FSD field catalog repeats the same eight write_off fields in seven sections and holds none of those four, and the Logical Data Model's write_off holds none of them either. The behaviour the committee and the team exercise therefore has nowhere stated to be recorded.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-07, R-WO-09, R-WO-17, R-WO-18; FSD S7 A2.4.3.2, A2.6.3.2, A2.7.3.2, A2.8.3.2, A2.12.3.2, A2.14.3.2, A2.16.3.2 field catalog (case_id, decision_log_id, amount, tax_criteria_met, committee_date, posted_date, responsibility_center, cost_center); Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 write_off DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020.
proposed: Hold the removal reason, the review date, the decision reason and the pack reference as required fields of the committee and eligibility records, and fix their physical names with the DB story.

title: The pack is prepared by the write-off agent, and the matrix gives S7 no path to the agent service
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.3; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-05; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 20; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-20
section: A2.3 Prepare the write-off pack
description: R-WO-05 has the write-off agent prepare the pack from the balance, the provision carried, the route history, the legal and asset state and the residual, and the FSD names the agent as the actor. The agent runtime is P10 rwb-agent, with its policies, prompts, runs and guardrails. The connection matrix gives the S7 row no P10 cell and the S7 service contract on slide 20 names no agent call, so the capability the pack depends on has no owned path, and no source states what the pack holds when the agent is unavailable.
evidence: FSD S7 A2.3 intent and steps (write-off agent); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-05 (owner column 'Agent Runtime, Document Hub'); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (S7 row: no P10 cell), slide 20 (S7 OUT: Decision, Payment only); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 no S7 agent row; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-20 (agent client to the rwb-agent contract).
owner_role: Solution architect with the P10 owner
proposed: Carry the pack as product behaviour that the agent drafts under its contract with a template fallback inside 60 seconds, and take the call type as an open question; the pack, not the agent, is the product requirement.

title: Payment matching after charge-off is given to this module, while P8 owns payment and proceeds matching
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.15; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-37, R-WO-38, R-WO-39, R-WO-49; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 40 and 44
section: A2.15 Record a customer payment after charge-off
description: R-WO-37 posts a post charge-off payment as income and calculates the agency fee once the payment matches the case and the placement, R-WO-38 sends a payment that matches nothing to the exception list and R-WO-39 matches it later. Payment and proceeds matching, fees and posting are P8 rwb-payment's own capability, with JOB-07 payment matching run there on AceDataReady, and ProceedsMatched (EV-25) is published to rwb-writeoff. Two services therefore appear to match the same payment.
evidence: FSD S7 A2.15 and R-WO-37 to R-WO-39; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 40 (P8 owns payment and proceeds matching, fees, bookings, posting files), slide 44 (JOB-07 payment matching on rwb-payment), slide 43 (EV-25 ProceedsMatched, consumer rwb-writeoff).
owner_role: Solution architect with the P8 owner
proposed: Consume ProceedsMatched as the match and record the recovery, the income and the agency fee here, hold the unmatched payment in the exception list this module shows, and take the ownership of the initial match as an open question with the P8 owner.

title: Completeness is published to a channel the sources remove
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-42; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 45 and ADR-018; Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.11
section: A2.11 Reconcile the approved and posted populations

No source states where completeness is published after the removal.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-42 (systems 'Rules component, Power BI, Workbench scheduler'), R-WO-43; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 45 and ADR-018 (no data lake; reporting from events), slide 41 (P9 owns measures and regulatory reports); FSD S7 A2.11.

title: The write-off proposal screen has no stated owner and no stated route through the gateway
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Screens; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 and DP-19; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 endpoints
section: Screens: SCR-27 Write-off proposal
description: The FSD names one screen, SCR-27 Write-off proposal, for the monthly population, the pack per case and the removals with reasons. No source read here states which service owns the screen, and Architecture v5 gives every staff screen to gateway-bff as a composite route with one hop and a 2 s timeout. The composite route for SCR-27 is therefore undefined, and its data comes from this service, rwb-case and rwb-document.
evidence: FSD S7 Screens (SCR-27 only); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (gateway-bff: the only entry for staff screens; composes at most a few parallel calls), slide 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-19 (screen to gateway-bff composite route); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Endpoints (no screen row).
proposed: Serve SCR-27 through a gateway-bff composite route that joins this service's population and pack answer with the case and the document, and take the ownership of the screen as an open question so that no service is named as its owner by invention.

title: No approval is recorded for the BRD or the FSD this PRD is built from, and this version is Draft
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) document control; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 13; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5
section: Document control; section 13 Approval
description: The FSD's document control shows Status 'In review' and its sign-off table is empty, and the epic BRD's governance table is the only approval record in the sources read. No Product Owner decision and no FDA decision exists for either document in this run, so the PRD cannot inherit an approved baseline and cannot be approved in this run.
evidence: FSD S7 document control (Status: In review) and Document sign-off (four empty rows); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 13 (governance and approval); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 1.
proposed: Carry the PRD as Draft, leave the approval table empty, and record the missing approval as an assumption so that no approval is claimed for a document nobody signed.
